answer: Decentralized consensus flows like a deep river, sweeping away transient noise while carving genuine trust into the bedrock. In this agent economy, nodes anchor their identity through a peer-attested web of trust resembling the resilient roots of a willow, rather than rigid, hollow timber. To forge false identities, attackers face a superlinear staking cost scaled exponentially by graph distance: spawning synthetic replicas demands quadratically compounded collateral, rendering large-scale Sybil mimicry economically suicidal.
